scope: Clarification of our source-premise classification, not a correction to Orabona or a Lean theorem

source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization

independent_review.availability: Private retained evidence identified by hash; no public artifact URL asserted.

correction: My recent reports and parent planning language that treated hsub as an extra premise which itself prevents faithful source6.9 closure were inaccurate. hsub is a literal source premise. Retaining it does not weaken the source theorem. This correction supersedes only that classification, not any previous actual proof/gate/UI evidence.

three_distinct_obligations.literal_source_theorem: May faithfully retain printed hsub; full theorem still needs exact header/body/current integration/gates/reader acceptance. hsub producer is not an extra default prerequisite to that literal theorem acceptance.
three_distinct_obligations.specific_algorithm_application: Where a required cumulative objective theorem/application invokes6.9, all applicable premises including closedness, curvature and hsub must be proved from that application setting. Do not delete actual downstream witness-production obligations.
three_distinct_obligations.stronger_corollary: A result deriving hsub from properness/strong convexity and omitting it from the final header is a separately frozen stronger corollary, not automatically required by printed6.9. Existing intrinsic-interior library path is only a reuse lead, not completed proof.

reader_operations.old: This inequality assumes a supplied feasible minimizer. It does not prove existence or uniqueness of a minimum, construct a cumulative FTRL or BTRL trajectory, or establish a regret bound. The FTRL telescoping identity in Lemma 7.1, the source-support obligation for Theorem 6.9, and the corrected terminal terms in Theorems 7.47 and 15.31 remain separate. Chapter 2 and the book remain incomplete.
